subtitle: Coins, Water and Law in the Reign of Budshah

panels.shot: dramatic close-up of a weathered silver coin held between royal fingers, Srinagar bazaar faintly blurred in the background
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands in soft Kashmiri light, holding up a gleaming silver sasnu, its script catching the sun while distant traders and villagers watch in hushed expectation.

dialogue.text: In the hand of Zain-ul-Abidin, Budshah of Kashmir, a small silver sasnu from 1438 decides the price of bread, the power of taxmen, and the quiet safety of every village lane.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर के बुज्शाह ज़ैनुलआबिदीन के हाथ में 1438 का छोटा चाँदी सास्नु – वही रोटी का भाव, महसूल की ताकत और हर गली की मुट्ठीभर सुरक्षा तय करता है।

panels.shot: museum-style macro shot of an actual silver sasnu lying on dark fabric, inscriptions and date glinting under a sharp shaft of light
panels.action: An ancient silver sasnu rests on worn black cloth, its Kashmiri mint legends and AH 842 date delicately lit, surrounded by shadow as if the past leans in.

dialogue.text: The silver sasnu survives, struck at Kashmir’s mint in AH 842, 1438–39. Tiny and silent, it proves one thing: Budshah’s promises were stamped into metal.

i18n.hi: चाँदी का सास्नु बचा रहा, कश्मीर के टकसाल में AH 842, 1438–39 में ढला। नन्हा, खामोश, पर साबित यही: बुज्शाह के वादे धातु पर मुहर थे।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of the royal audience hall in Srinagar, low-angle on the throne with nobles and officials assembled
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin sits on his throne in a carved wooden hall, nobles and tax officials arrayed before him as he studies a tray of different, uneven coins laid out by scribes.

dialogue.text: When Zain-ul-Abidin took power, Kashmir’s coins were a tangle—debased, uneven, distrusted. Markets murmured, taxmen preyed, and every deal carried doubt.

i18n.hi: ज़ैनुलआबिदीन के आते ही कश्मीर के सिक्के उलझन थे—घटिया, बेढंगे, बेऐतबार। बाज़ार गुनगुनाते, महसूलखोर झपटते, हर सौदा शक में डूबा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Zain-ul-Abidin in council, examining scales and coins, officials around him
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin leans forward at a council table, weighing old coins on brass scales while a worried merchant and a stern tax collector watch his judgment.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: If the coin lies, the price follows. If the price lies, the people starve.

i18n.hi: सिक्का झूठ बोले, तो भाव भी झूठा होता है। भाव झूठा हो, तो लोग भूखे मरते हैं।

panels.shot: interior of royal mint, dynamic mid-shot, Zain-ul-Abidin inspecting craftsmen and dies
panels.action: Inside the Kashmir mint, Zain-ul-Abidin stands among furnaces and anvils as engravers carve dies, molten metal is poured, and fresh round blanks are stacked for striking.

dialogue.text: He turned to the mint. Under his eye, Kashmir struck regulated silver sasnus—consistent weight, clear legend, one authority. The state’s word hardened into coin.

i18n.hi: वह टकसाल की तरफ मुड़ा। उसकी नज़र में कश्मीर ने तयशुदा चाँदी सास्नु ढाले—एक सा वज़न, साफ लिखावट, एक ही हुकूमत। राज्य की बात सिक्के में सख्त हो गई।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of coins being struck, Zain-ul-Abidin in background overseeing
panels.action: A mint worker raises a hammer over a die resting on a glowing blank, while behind him Zain-ul-Abidin watches, hands clasped, as rows of new silver coins shine on a cloth.

dialogue.text: Majumdar and Hasan note how his standardized currency steadied trade. Traders from Bengal to Sindh could trust a Kashmiri coin and measure their risk clearly.

i18n.hi: मजुमदार और हसन लिखते हैं कि उसकी एकरूप करंसी ने कारोबार सँभाला। बंगाल से सिंध तक के सौदागर कश्मीरी सिक्के पर यकीन कर जोखिम साफ तौल सके।

panels.shot: busy Srinagar market street, mid-wide, emphasis on daily commerce
panels.action: In a bustling Srinagar bazaar, shopkeepers weigh silver sasnu coins on small scales as women buy grain, shawl sellers bargain, and a money-changer sits alert at his mat.

dialogue.text: In Srinagar’s lanes, the change was felt in weighs and measures. With stable sasnus, grain dealers, shawl sellers, and caravan-men could set prices without fear of sudden loss.

i18n.hi: श्रीनगर की गलियों में तौल–माप से असर दिखा। स्थिर सास्नु से अनाजवाले, शालफ़रोश और क़ाफ़िला-मर्द बेख़ौफ़ दाम तय कर पाए, अचानक घाटे का डर मिटा।

panels.shot: royal council chamber, wide shot with scrolls and revenue officials
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin presides over a revenue council, officials unroll land registers and tax schedules while one nervous provincial officer kneels, clutching a petition.

dialogue.text: But coin alone was not enough. Across the valleys, petty officers piled unlawful cesses onto the crown’s share. Budshah moved to curb every unauthorised provincial tax.

i18n.hi: पर सिर्फ सिक्का काफी नहीं था। वादियों में छोटे अफ़सर ताज के हिस्से पर नाजायज़ लगान चढ़ाते रहे। बुज्शाह ने हर बिन-इजाज़त सूबाई टैक्स काटने की ठान ली।

panels.shot: close three-quarter shot of Zain-ul-Abidin dictating an order to a scribe
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin dictates calmly to a court scribe, who writes on paper as two provincial officials stand stiffly, hearing the new limits on what they may collect.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: The Sultan’s due is fixed. Beyond that, no man may take a single sasnu.

i18n.hi: सुल्तान का हक़ तय है। उसके आगे एक भी सास्नु कोई नहीं ले सकता।

panels.shot: rural village scene, wide shot showing fields, houses, and a small gathering under a chinar tree
panels.action: In a Kashmiri village, peasants gather under a great chinar as a royal envoy reads a decree, while in the background terraced fields stretch along an irrigation channel.

dialogue.text: Hasan records his effort to restrain revenue pressure. In villages, envoys carried orders: the crown would protect cultivation, and officers would be checked by law.

i18n.hi: हसन लिखता है कि उसने महसूल की मार रोकने की कोशिश की। गाँवों में फ़रमान पहुँचे: ताज खेती की हिफ़ाज़त करेगा, और अफ़सर कानून से बाँधे जाएँगे।

panels.shot: daytime village lane, mid-shot of a tense scene with locals and a minor official
panels.action: A minor tax collector argues with villagers in a narrow lane as a royal officer steps between them, holding up a parchment that lists lawful dues and forbids extra demands.

dialogue.text: Abuses did not vanish, but the centre drew a line. With currency discipline and revenue rules, it became possible for a farmer to know what he truly owed.

i18n.hi: जुल्म मिटे नहीं, पर केंद्र ने एक रेखा खींच दी। करंसी की लगाम और राजस्व के उसूलों से किसान को समझ आने लगा कि उसका असली बकाया कितना है।

panels.shot: exterior of karkhana workshop, wide shot showing looms, paper making and carpentry
panels.action: A large karkhana complex hums with activity: artisans weave shawls, press paper sheets, knot carpets and prepare saffron, while a steward records production near the entrance.

dialogue.text: Inside state karkhanas, Budshah nurtured crafts—saffron, shawls, paper, carpets. Regulated coin and fair dues turned skill into stable livelihood, not gamble.

i18n.hi: राज्य के कारखानों में बुज्शाह ने हुनर सँवारा—केसर, शाल, कागज़, कालीन। पक्का सिक्का और जायज़ लगान ने हुनर को रोज़गार बनाया, जुआ नहीं।

panels.shot: trade caravan on mountain pass, wide shot with distant mountains and loaded animals
panels.action: A caravan winds along a mountain pass, pack animals laden with shawls and saffron casks, as a Kashmiri official exchanges greetings with merchants bound for Khorasan and Tibet.

dialogue.text: Mahajan notes Kashmir’s trade links—to Bengal, Gujarat, Sindh, Tibet, Timurid Khorasan, even Egypt. Trustworthy coin and predictable dues made faraway deals possible.

i18n.hi: महेजन कश्मीर की रगों को दिखाता है—बंगाल, गुजरात, सिंध, तिब्बत, तैमूरी खुरासान, यहाँ तक कि मिस्र तक। भरोसेमंद सिक्का और तयशुदा लगान ने दूर के सौदे मुमकिन किए।

panels.shot: village assembly scene, wide shot, emphasis on collective gathering
panels.action: Villagers sit in a circle by a stream as a qazi and a state officer address them, explaining that the village as a whole will answer for crimes committed within its bounds.

dialogue.text: Majumdar points to another discipline: villages became collectively responsible for crimes in their bounds. Law stepped into the lane, not just the court.

i18n.hi: मजुमदार एक और उसूल पर उँगली रखता है: गाँव अपनी हदों में जुर्म के लिए मिलकर ज़िम्मेदार हुए। कानून सिर्फ अदालत नहीं, गली तक उतर आया।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Zain-ul-Abidin hearing a case, villagers and accused present
panels.action: In a modest rural court, Zain-ul-Abidin listens as villagers and an accused man stand before him, the community spokesman bowing and accepting the village’s share of responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: When wrong walks freely, it is the road that must answer with him.

i18n.hi: जब नाइंसाफ़ी खुले आम चले, तो उसके साथ रास्ता भी जवाबदेह होता है।

panels.shot: night-time interior, contemplative close-up of Zain-ul-Abidin beside a lamp and a coin
panels.action: By lamplight, Zain-ul-Abidin sits alone, turning a silver sasnu between his fingers, a map of Kashmir spread before him marked with markets, canals, and villages.

dialogue.text: His reign is remembered for gentleness, for the name Budshah. Yet behind the praise lay hard lines—currency rules, tax limits, village liability—that held prosperity in shape.

i18n.hi: उसका दौर नरमी के लिए, ‘बुज्शाह’ नाम के लिए याद है। पर इस तारीफ़ के पीछे सख़्त लकीरें थीं—करंसी के उसूल, टैक्स की हदें, गाँव की ज़िम्मेदारी—जिन्होंने तरक़्क़ी को आकार दिया।

panels.shot: split visual: museum coin close-up fading into a modern Kashmiri street scene
panels.action: The ancient silver sasnu glows in close-up, then subtly blends into a modern Kashmiri street with shops and homes, echoing the long shadow of old rules over new lives.

dialogue.text: Today the sasnu is just a relic in glass. Yet it reminds us that when money is steady and law restrains greed, small lives—then and now—finally have room to breathe.

i18n.hi: आज वो सास्नु सिर्फ काँच के पीछे की निशानी है। पर याद दिलाता है कि जब रुपया ठहरा हुआ हो और कानून लालच को बाँधे, तो छोटी ज़िंदगियाँ—तब भी, अब भी—साँस लेने की जगह पा लेती हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Coins, Water and Law in the Reign of Budshah
subtitle_i18n.hi: बुज्शाह के दौर में सिक्का, पानी और कानून
